item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Warmer Colours Only

turns.text: Make it warmer—just the colours, please. Don't change anything in the picture.

item.tests: Tests interpreting 'warmer' as a colour-temperature adjustment rather than a scene or weather change.

answer_sheet.Meaning of warmer: A warmer colour balance only, not different weather, a new sunset or added objects.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: Keep the original 16:9 composition; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Text or other edits: No text and no changes beyond the colours.

must_haves: The image has a visibly warmer colour balance than the source.
The same mountains, pine trees, clouds and lake remain in their original positions.
The lake's reflections and surface details retain their original structure.
No sun, sunset, extra clouds or other scene elements are added.
Framing, geometry and image detail remain unchanged apart from colour.

turns.text: Make it warmer—just the colours, please. Don't change anything in the picture.
turns.agent:
I couldn't make the edit. Magic Hour turned the request down because your account doesn't have enough credits, so nothing was created and no credits were used. I'd already picked the cheapest option on the free plan (flux-2-klein at 640px, from 5 credits per image), so trying again won't help until you have more credits.

What you can do:

1. **Add credits to your Magic Hour account**, then tell me and I'll run the same edit: a warmer white balance with soft golden and amber tones, keeping everything else the same. One thing to know first: this tool redraws the whole image, and on the free plan the result is at most 640px wide. So small details, like branches or reflections, may come out a little different, and the image will be smaller than your original.
2. **Use a basic photo editor instead.** Since you want only the colours changed, this may be the better choice anyway. In your phone's Photos app, Lightroom, Snapseed or GIMP, move the **Warmth / Temperature** slider up a little (try +10 to +20), and maybe raise **Tint** slightly towards magenta. This changes only the colours, keeps every pixel of the picture in place, keeps your full resolution and costs nothing.
